newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Robinson "honoured" by U.N. human rights job.
newsitem.headline: Robinson "honoured" by U.N. human rights job.

text.p: Ireland's President Mary Robinson said on Thursday that she was very honoured to be appointed United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights.
"I deeply appreciate the trust and confidence which the (U.N.) Secretary-General has placed in me," she said in a statement.
"I am greatly indebted to all those who supported my candidature, especially to the Irish government and officials in the Department of Foreign Affairs who spared no effort in promoting it."
She said Secretary-General Kofi Annan had telephoned her on Wednesday afternoon to ask that she accept the job in time for the United Nations General Assembly meeting in mid-September.
This will mean that Ireland will either have to find an agreed candidate to take over her position or hold an election to find a successor ahead of November, when her term expires.

Former Prime Minister Albert Reynolds, Northern Ireland peace broker John Hume and Maire Geoghean-Quinn, a one-time Justice Minister of the Fianna Fail party, are among names tipped as potential successors.
Outgoing Deputy Irish Prime Minister Dick Spring said in a statement that the choice of Robinson for the Human Rights position had been an easy task.
"Her appointment is a great honour for President Robinson and for Ireland," he said in a statement.
"When the President announced she would not seek re-election and was interested in the U.N., we put together a campaign committee in the Department of Foreign Affairs here at the highest level.

"I am glad to say that when we approached all the embassies they recognised the qualities and calibre of President Robinson, and in that respect it was an easy job for us to do," said Spring, leader of the Irish Labour Party of which Robinson is a member.
